In today's digital environment, having great graphic design skills is essential, and good designers are often in demand.

Enrolling in an online course to learn directly from experts is the simplest way to grasp graphic design.

‍What are the best free graphic design courses online?

‍There are lots of great graphic design courses you can get online. This collection of online graphic design courses is completely free.

But with so many online courses to choose from, it can be difficult to decide which ones are worth your time.

In this article, I've compiled a list of the 10 best free graphics design courses available on some of the most popular creative learning platforms, including Skillshare, Coursera, Udemy, and more.

These courses range from the fundamentals of graphic design, such as typography, composition, and color, to more advanced topics and industry tips and tricks, depending on your aims and interests.

How to Learn Graphic Design?

Graphic design is the process of graphically presenting information, so you must first learn to communicate well.

The reality is that breaking into the graphic design industry isn't as simple as it appears— there's a lot of competition.

How to become a true skilled graphic designer?

Anyone with a little understanding of Photoshop or Illustrator nowadays claims to be a graphic designer.

However, being a skilled graphic designer necessitates far more than a working knowledge of Adobe products.


You must first grasp graphic design history and where it came from in order to become a competent communicator.

Then you must learn how to successfully communicate using various parts of visual language.

You have all you need when you combine your own ingenuity and expressiveness.

Here are the five basic steps to help you get the most out of your learning curve:

  1. Research graphic design history—Knowing the history and present situation of the graphic design industry can provide you with the confidence you need to succeed as a designer.
  2. Understand core design principles—To make your designs more creative and compelling, you'll need to understand key design principles as a designer.
  3. Master graphic design process—Working with your graphic design clients will be more efficient and effective if you follow a systematic procedure.
  4. Follow great designers—To improve your talents and become more creative, you should surround yourself with excellent designers, follow them, and replicate their work.
  5. Build a portfolio and get hired—If you want to get employed and land huge assignments, you'll need to develop your own style.

Like in any discipline, you'll need to learn the fundamentals before moving on to more advanced material.

This 36-minute online class teaches you how to apply real-world examples in your design work.

I was fortunate enough to host Ellen Lupton on my podcast, where we discussed how to use storytelling in graphic design work.

‍The course also includes a hands-on project that you can use to practice your skills.

This course is excellent for graphic design students and creatives who want to build a solid foundation in graphic design.

Every step of the way, you'll get a sense of how designers think: from mood boards to typography basics, color theory, and everything in between.

This course is for you if you only want to dip your toes in the water to acquire a better knowledge of how designers think.

Customizing type is a vital skill for all levels of graphic designers.

Master typography for every branding, logo, and identity project.

This course has around 31,000 students registered.

Join design icon Aaron Draplin as he shares tried and true techniques for customizing type.

Draplin shows you how to manage the shapes, in-between spaces, and relationships of the letters you're dealing with instead of using "default" typeface settings.

‍In this 90-minute class, you'll watch as Draplin searches for antique typographic sources.

He will then create his own type treatments to make items for his favorite hometown of Portland.

For beginners, this is the most comprehensive graphic design course available.

Despite the fact that the lessons in this course are extensive, Derrick had to compress everything about graphic design into less than 2 hours.

This course will teach you how to create and use mockups in Adobe Photoshop, which is an important skill for showcasing your design work.

You'll learn how to make your ideas look fresh and original, as well as how to use fundamental design "tricks" to give your mockups a professional and convincing appearance.

5. Graphic Design Specialization

The purpose of the Graphic Design Specialization is to provide students with a set of transferable formal and conceptual skills in graphic design.

Learn the fundamentals of graphic design and apply them to a thorough branding project.

‍Michael Worthington is a co-founder of Counterspace in LA, a graphic design firm that specializes in editorial and identity work for cultural clientele.

This five-course sequence introduces students to the core skills needed to create complex graphic design.

This foundational skill set will prepare students for formal graphic design courses.

A capstone project brings together the skills learned in each course as well as peer feedback to produce a final branding project fit for a professional portfolio.

This is a required course for students interested in learning more about visual culture and analysis, and no prior experience is necessary.

Learn everything you need to know about graphic design fundamentals.

This course will teach you the essential principles of graphic design through visual examples such as imagemaking, typography, composition, color and shape work.

If you want to be a designer, you must be a creator and a communicator, this course will provide you with plenty of practice activities and projects.

7. Introduction to Typography

The art of changing the visual form of language to enrich and control its meaning is known as typography.

As part of the Graphic Design Specialization course, learning the fundamentals of typography is a must.

‍Anther Kiley is a designer and design educator based in Providence, Rhode Island.

Typography predates modern graphic design by around 500 years; it's full of rules, conventions, and jargon, but it's still a fun place to experiment and express yourself.

In this course, you will analyze, name, and quantify the features of letterforms in this tough introductory course.

You will also delve into the fascinating historical, cultural, and aesthetic backgrounds of well-known typefaces.

You will also learn the practical issues that come up when choosing and mixing typefaces by going over tried-and-true rules and best practices for establishing type.

Course details:

  • Experience Level: Beginner
  • Language: English, Arabic, French, Portuguese, Italian, Vietnamese, German, Russian, Spanish
  • Price: Free from CalArts
  • Category: Arts and Humanities

What you will learn:

  • Conduct a typesetting exercise that is peer-reviewed

8. Introduction to Imagemaking

Imagemaking is a fluid and engaging area of graphic design that emerges from practice and process.

This course is designed for both experienced and novice photographers.

‍Gail Swanlund is a writer and graphic designer.

If there is one guideline you must follow in this course, it is that you will not become a graphic designer alone by viewing videos.

In  this course, the emphasis is on making, and you are expected to commit significant time and mental energy to that activity.

The first half of the course gives you the chance to play around with imagemaking and develop your visual vocabulary.

Your tasks may produce something absolutely unknown now or in the future, which is the main purpose of this course.

9. Ideas From the History of Graphic Design

This course is presented from the standpoint of modern design, with the goal of connecting concepts that shaped design practice from the 1850s to the 1960s to how designers think today.

‍Louise Sandhaus is a former CalArts Graphic Design Program Director and current faculty member.

This short survey course concentrates on four significant periods or themes in Western design history.

This is a required course for students interested in learning more about visual culture and analysis, or for rising designers joining the profession.

All public visual communications are included in the definition and practice of graphic design, which is a global profession.

Students will gain a grasp of the origins of today's wide range of design practice.

10. Brand New Brand

This course is the capstone to the Graphic Design Specialization, and it allows you to combine your knowledge and talents into a single project.

From concept to development to presentation, this course walks you through the full design process.

‍Michael Worthington, a faculty member of the Program in Graphic Design at the California Institute of the Arts, will be instructing this course as well.

You will be building and giving a visual identity to an imagined start-up company, as well as applying that visual identity to a variety of forms.

You'll also create a logotype and an accompanying graphic palette to visually represent your business.

This course will also teach you to use that design in a variety of applications to see it in action.

You will also learn the practical issues that come up when choosing and mixing typefaces by going over tried-and-true rules and best practices for establishing type.

How to Choose a Graphic Design Course

Whether you're new to graphic design or have some experience, there's something for everyone on my list.

There are so many online courses to choose from that it can be tough to know which one is appropriate for you.

How to choose a graphic design course?

Graphic design is a broad term that includes a variety of sub-disciplines such as typography, color theory, layout and grid, and so on.

Depending on where you are in your career, you may want to brush up on the fundamentals with some beginner courses or complement your knowledge with more advanced courses for experts.

Graphic design is a constantly changing field, with new tools and techniques appearing on a monthly basis.

As a result, you must constantly update your skills and seek out new opportunities.

Conclusions

These days, becoming a graphic designer does not have to be done in school.

‍Learn the basics of graphic design in the comfort of your own home.

There are so many courses available online these days that attending design school for years makes little sense.

You would be much better off spending this time learning from some of the industry's greatest designers, honing your style, and expanding your portfolio.

I guarantee that if you take at least a few of these graphic design courses from my list, you will become an expert in your field.
